courses.description: Students in this class will take a virtual trip around the world to find out what music is like around the globe! From salsa music to Mongolian Metal to yodeling and K-pop, we explore the characteristics of music from different countries and cultures. In this class, we will learn about the instruments, rhythms, songs and dances associated with world music. We will explore what music from different parts of the world has in common and what makes it distinct. Students in this class should be prepared to listen to music and watch videos, participate in class discussions, and play percussion instruments (no previous experience required).
courses.fulfills_text: A graduation credit in the arts can be earned in music classes.

courses.description: This course is designed to explore the history of Rock ‘n Roll by analyzing, studying and performing its songs. We will be learning about cultural influences on Rock, listening to music representing different stages in its development, and performing songs by major artists. Students will be advancing individual guitar skills for both rhythm and lead guitar as well as discovering the basics of harmony used in Rock ‘n Roll. Guitars will be supplied for students.

courses.description: Visual and Performing Arts Academy students in a music strand must take this class. This course is designed to give students a deep understanding of three fundamental aspects of music theory: rhythm, melody and harmony. A variety of composition projects are designed to follow instruction in these three areas, allowing students to create meaning of the information and apply it in authentic ways. Noteflight music notation program enables students to compose, edit and share their work. Inside Music web-based composition instructional units are used extensively. This rigorous class is best suited for students with some background in music. It is highly recommended for students planning to further pursue music after high school. Topics uncovered include meter, rhythm, time signatures, clefs, pitch notation, major and minor scales, melodic analysis, connections of text to music, motive, form, chords (diatonic and non-diatonic), connection of melody to harmony, chord progressions and analysis.

courses.description: This course provides students with instruction in Health Education according to the Vermont Comprehensive Health Education Program. It is designed to meet the needs of students in accordance with their stages of physical, mental, and social development as well as promote healthy choices. Health Education addresses current issues through units on nutrition & physical activity; bullying & violence prevention; suicide prevention; alcohol, tobacco & other drugs; human sexuality; and healthy relationships. An emphasis is placed on activities designed to build self-efficacy around health skills including decision making skills, goal setting, communication skills, and health advocacy.

courses.description: Recommended: Mentoring & Leadership This course builds upon concepts learned in Health (9th/10th grade). Students in Teaching Health in Elementary Schools will explore concepts of mentoring and teaching, and complete a practical application at local elementary schools in order to promote Health Standards of the Vermont Comprehensive Health Education Program. Students will choose a health focus area (nutrition, injury prevention, drugs/medicine, infectious disease, mental/emotional health and relationship health) and develop age appropriate activities & curriculum to implement with elementary students. Activities will also emphasize skills including decision making skills, goal setting, and communication skills. Grading for this course will be based on the successful planning of several health lessons for elementary grades AND visiting those classrooms and teaching the lessons. Students in this course must exhibit a very high level of responsibility, as they will be expected to travel outside of BUHS during regular school hours. Transportation will be required, or parent permission to travel with someone else in a personal vehicle.

courses.course_name: CPR, First Aid & Wilderness First Aid
courses.description: In this hands-on, practical course, students will learn critical life-saving skills that can be applied in everyday situations and emergency scenarios. The curriculum covers three main areas: CPR (Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation) & AED, basic First Aid, and Wilderness First Aid. Students will gain proficiency in recognizing medical emergencies, using an AED, performing CPR, and providing first aid for common injuries and illnesses. After covering basic first aid techniques, additional emphasis will be placed on first aid techniques in outdoor and remote environments, where professional medical help may be delayed. Key topics include wound care, splinting, hypothermia, heat-related illnesses, snake bites, and other wilderness-specific emergencies. By the end of the course, students will be prepared to respond confidently in both urban and wilderness settings, with the ability to stabilize injured individuals until professional medical help arrives. The course includes certification in CPR and First Aid, ensuring students are well-equipped to handle a wide range of emergency situations. Key Skills Covered: ● Using an AED when one is available ● Performing CPR on adults, children, and infants ● Recognizing and treating common medical emergencies ● Administering first aid for cuts, burns, fractures, and sprains ● Wilderness-specific first aid techniques (e.g., treating hypothermia, insect bites, and dehydration) ● Responding to environmental hazards like extreme heat or cold Grading in this class will be a reflection of active demonstration of learned skills, scores on content-based quizzes, and performance-based role playing of medical emergencies. Active participation will be required.

courses.description: The Vermont Agency of Education (AOE) has established a number of programs through which Vermont high school students can earn both high school and college credit for certain courses they take while in high school. ● “Concurrent” Dual Enrollment (DE) courses are courses taught at BUHS by BUHS faculty who are also adjunct professors with the partner college. These courses are designated in the Programs of Study and on BUHS transcript with an * after the course title. ● “Fast Forward” DE courses are courses taught at WRCC by WRCC faculty who are also adjunct professors with the partner college. They are also designated with an * in the program of studies and on student transcripts. ● “Traditional” DE Courses are taken at the Partner College, either online or on the college campus. These courses are designated by a + symbol in the program of studies and on student transcripts. For a list of eligible AOE Partner Colleges please visit: https://education.vermont.gov/dual-enrollment
